summary: Carded from an MPI-387 F2 side-trace: a GPU-less first run cannot reach RunPod because the non-dismissible engine-install modal covers the only UI that enables it. Placed second in To do, directly under MPI-385, so the deliberate top-of-board stays put.

Implementation started. Product decisions taken by the user first, recorded in plan.md: a NEW skipLocalEngine flag (not autoConnectOnStart, which bills a Pod at every launch), always visible on the setup phase (no gpu.vendor gate - MPI-387 F2 proved detection misses Iris/UHD/HD by design), a link on the modal plus a RunPod setup video link, and re-arm via a settings toggle because Settings has no engine-install section.

Plan and 6-item checklist derived. Trap the brief missed and the plan now names: the boot gate is an await new Promise resolved ONLY by engine:ready (shell.js:268-274), so hiding the modal alone hangs boot behind an invisible gate - the hatch emits engine:install-skipped rather than faking engine:ready.

Code complete across 5 files plus a new test. Three traps the brief did not name, all silent: normalizeRunpodConfig is a WHITELIST running on read AND write so the DEFAULT_RUNPOD_CONFIG entry alone would have been stripped every save/load (same class as MPI-370 requirementsDrop); the boot gate is an await new Promise resolved ONLY by engine:ready so hiding the modal would hang boot behind an invisible gate (hatch emits engine:install-skipped instead of faking ready); and the hatch must write through state.runpodConfig not Storage.setRunpodConfig or state goes stale and the next state write clobbers the flag. Deliberately NOT auto-opening Settings - first launch also runs the 18+/changelog chain and Overlays.reset, which is the MPI-333 double-backdrop bug. Suite 279/279, eslint clean, and the new test was NEGATIVE-CONTROLLED (all 4 cases fail with the whitelist line removed). In-app verification still open - needs a machine where needsInstall is true.

Scope extended on the users call, plus the video link swapped to the direct YouTube URL (https://youtu.be/drpZOrMDEq8) whose description already carries the docs links. The hatch made no-engine-at-all reachable for the first time: with no Pod connected dispatch falls to LOCAL, so every graph op (generate, SAM3, upscale, right-click Describe) would die on the routes/comfy.js:343 guard with Provision engine first - the opposite of the advice a deliberate skipper needs. Gated at PROJECT ENTRY rather than sprinkling guards through Gallery/History: one choke point covers every in-workspace tool at once. Follows the existing _blockedByDownloadMode precedent exactly, same two call sites. Cheapest-first so the common path does zero I/O, and fails OPEN on a version-check error. Sweep: openProject has exactly 2 live call sites, both gated; drag-drop only adds to the grid; forceLocal is never structural (only the users own PromptBox override). Known consequence, users call: a cloud user cannot browse past projects offline without connecting. Suite still 279/279, eslint clean.

Gate REDESIGNED with the user, then the re-arm added. Gate now sits on the THREE doors out of the landing page - open a project, open the Model Library, open the App Library - via a new shared js/services/engineGate.js. The fine-grained alternative was costed and rejected: gating what FAILS needs Gallery card open, App Generate, PromptBox Run, right-click Describe and one more per tool added later, five and growing. Gating entry costs nothing because Open in file system is a LANDING-page right-click, so every image stays reachable without opening a project. models:open/apps:open gated on the LISTENER not the nav emitters so the Gallery radial is covered too. Re-arm: toggling the skip OFF emits engine:install-request, shell re-runs version-check and shows the install modal; pressing Skip on it flips the Settings switch back ON. Trap: the modal only EMITS engine:ready and never hides itself - the boot gate did that and had unsubscribed - so the post-boot path wires its own close for both outcomes or the modal would sit there forever after a successful install. Suite 279/279, eslint clean.
USER-VERIFIED in the app and closed. Escape hatch on the engine-install modal ships with a no-engine gate on the three landing-page doors and an immediate re-arm when the skip is switched back off.
